claim: niri's IPC socket is created at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/niri.{wayland_socket_name}.{pid}.sock — the directory is BaseDirs::new().runtime_dir() (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, falling back to /tmp) and the filename embeds the compositor's wayland socket name and PID, e.g. /run/user/1000/niri.wayland-1.2474.sock.
stance_target: gap-06: resolving NIRI_SOCKET's filesystem location from primary source
scope_conditions: niri-wm/niri main branch, 2026; requires a wayland socket name (nested/TTY instances without one create no IPC socket — socket_path is None)
quoted_support: let socket_name = format!("niri.{wayland_socket_name}.{}.sock", process::id()); let mut socket_path = socket_dir(); socket_path.push(socket_name); let listener = UnixListener::bind(&socket_path)

claim: niri's IPC server performs no peer-credential authentication: the source contains no SO_PEERCRED/PeerCredentials check, no chmod, no umask manipulation — access to the socket is gated purely by the filesystem permissions of the socket inode inside the (0700, user-owned) XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so a same-UID process (e.g. a User=io system service) can connect; other UIDs cannot.
stance_target: gap-06: whether a process outside the session can reach NIRI_SOCKET — yes, if it runs as the same user
scope_conditions: out-of-session process must run as the session user; path discoverability requires knowing the PID (embedded in filename)
quoted_support: socket_dir() = BaseDirs::new().as_ref().and_then(|x| x.runtime_dir()).map(|x| x.to_owned()).unwrap_or_else(env::temp_dir) — with no permission or credential handling anywhere in IpcServer::start or on_new_ipc_client

claim: niri's event-stream IPC has a bounded 64-event buffer per client — a client that cannot drain events fast enough gets dropped, a hard capacity constraint for any fleet agent consuming niri's event stream from a busy session.
stance_target: fleet-agent design constraint when consuming niri IPC event streams
quoted_support: If an event stream client fails to read events fast enough that we accumulate more than this number in our buffer, we drop that event stream client. const EVENT_STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 64;
